name: Constructing Tests
description: Let's denote a m -free matrix as a binary (that is, consisting of only 1 's and 0 's) matrix such that every square submatrix of size m × m of this matrix contains at least one zero. Consider the following problem: You are given two integers n and m . You have to construct an m -free square matrix of size n × n such that the number of 1 's in this matrix is maximum possible . Print the maximum possible number of 1 's in such matrix. You don't have to solve this problem. Instead, you have to construct a few tests for it. You will be given t numbers x 1 , x 2 , ..., x t . For every , find two integers n i and m i ( n i ≥ m i ) such that the answer for the aforementioned problem is exactly x i if we set n = n i and m = m i .
input_specification: The first line contains one integer t ( 1 ≤ t ≤ 100 ) — the number of tests you have to construct. Then t lines follow, i -th line containing one integer x i ( 0 ≤ x i ≤ 10 9 ). Note that in hacks you have to set t = 1 .
output_specification: For each test you have to construct, output two positive numbers n i and m i ( 1 ≤ m i ≤ n i ≤ 10 9 ) such that the maximum number of 1 's in a m i -free n i × n i matrix is exactly x i . If there are multiple solutions, you may output any of them; and if this is impossible to construct a test, output a single integer - 1 .
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 938C — Constructing Tests [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
